dedupe_keys.name: downdetector crowdsourced outage reports and downdetector explorer ookla

description: Downdetector is a website, owned by Ookla since 2018, that detects outages of telecom, internet, cloud and online services from reports submitted by the public. Users say when a service such as a mobile operator, broadband provider, bank or streaming platform is not working; Downdetector combines these with other signals such as social media mentions and web performance indicators, compares them against each service's normal baseline and declares an incident when reports rise well above it. According to secondary sources it handles more than 25 million user reports a month and covers services in 64 countries as of 2025, and news outlets and regulators often quote its report counts during large outages. Free public pages show the last 24 hours of reports, a map and common problems for each service. Downdetector Explorer, the paid enterprise product, adds historical analytics, location-based reports, comparison between providers, alerts and an API. Coverage: 64 countries, services across telecom and online sectors, continuous since about 2012. Format and access: web pages free to view; historical data and API only under a paid Ookla contract, with no open licence. Caveats: reports measure user perception, not network state; counts depend on popularity and media attention; methods are proprietary. Simulation uses: detecting and timing outages for event catalogues, user-side impact of network failures and validating restoration curves. Related records: IODA and the Cloud Uptime Archive give open outage data, and regulator outage reports such as FCC NORS give operator views.
